items.text:
Alcaraz beat Shelton 7–6, 7–5 in the final to win the title, his fourth win against Shelton in 5 meetings. It was a tight match with few breaks of serve, decided by how each player handled the break points.

The first set had no break of serve but Alcaraz was under pressure more often. He saved 4 break points to hold for 2–2. Shelton saved 2 to hold for 4–3, then Alcaraz saved 2 more for 4–4 before he won the tiebreak. In the second set Shelton finally broke for 3–2 but Alcaraz broke back for 4–4. At 6–5 Shelton served to stay in the match and saved a first match point. Alcaraz needed only one more chance in that game to break again and win the set 7–5.

Alcaraz won it with his serve when it mattered most. He landed 72% of his first serves, well above his 64% average, so Shelton rarely got a second serve to attack on the big points. That is how Alcaraz saved every break point he faced in the first set. When he came forward he also won most of his points at the net.

Shelton had plenty of chances on return but took only one of them. His own first serve did not hurt Alcaraz enough. He won just 64% of the points behind it, compared with his 76% average, so he could not keep the pressure off his own service games in the second set.

All in all, a clutch win from Alcaraz, built on his serve under pressure and the all court game that makes him so dangerous, on an indoor court in Paris that plays at a medium pace. Credit to him: the title is his.

Alcaraz: W: 33 / UE: 27 | DR: 1.25

Shelton: W: 25 / UE: 26 | DR: 0.80
